title: Kingdom of Lunda
capsule: The Lunda Empire (also Ruund Empire) was a confederation of states spanning what is now the Katanga region of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, northeastern Angola, and northwestern Zambia, founded in the early 18th century under Mwata Yamvo Yaav a Yirung. At its apex in the 18th and early 19th centuries it controlled long-distance trade in copper, ivory, and enslaved people, connecting the interior to both the Atlantic and Indian Ocean coasts through tributary networks. Portuguese and later Belgian colonial encroachment progressively undermined Lunda sovereignty from the 1880s onward, and the state was fully absorbed into the Congo Free State by 1890.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Lunda territorial extent is reconstructed primarily from 19th-century Portuguese and Belgian travellers' accounts and oral traditions; pre-19th-century boundaries are estimated rather than documented.
